Prof. McCormack is a fantastic teacher all around. Her interest in the class material is evident from her enthusiasm and her ability to engage students with the topics and themes we discussed. She has always been very patient with us and encouraged us, and I enjoyed the classes and the assignments so much that I went around telling my friends about them! I particularly liked the creative bonus points assignment we were given, and I appreciated how her feedback was always thorough and fair; gently nudging us in the right direction if we strayed from the format or failed to critically engage with the text. During class hours she also always managed to get heated discussion going, and I don’t think there was anyone in the class who stayed silent the entire semester—class discussion was a blast in this course. And the presentation—consequent response paper we had to complete were very effective in getting us to dive really deep into the themes at hand. I don’t know what else to say, she really was a fantastic teacher and this class rocked majorly!
course: great course with some gay dressings

I don’t have anything negative to say about the course. The format managed to reach peak engagement—texts to read each week that follow a cohesive narrative (relevant to the way we discussed the imagined American West) presentations about said texts, insane class discussion all the time, podcast episodes to listen to, movies to watch (and she gave us handouts with questions to consider about the movie; to really think deep about the movie as we were watching it) and essays to write about them, a few optional assignments to give us a tiny grade boost at the end of the semester, and even the fact that the exam is in take-home format is perfect—the themes that we discuss in the class are too intersectional, complex, and nuanced to be able to write sufficiently on in a sit-in exam atmosphere; whereas the flexibility, extra time/space to work on the essay, and the ability to choose your own workspace, will do wonders for really delving deep into these critical issues. I genuinely can not think of a weakness of the course, or come up with a way to improve it.
